title: Buttons
summary: A button triggers an action; its label and visual hierarchy must predict its consequence and distinguish it from navigation.

MUST.text: Use a verb + object label such as “Save changes”; keep prominent actions to one or two per view.
Use native `<button>` for actions and `<a>` only for navigation.
Give icon-only buttons an accessible name (visible text or aria-label).
Provide a visible focus indicator and keyboard activation via Enter/Space.

SHOULD.text: Use a lower-emphasis style for secondary actions and require explicit consequence or confirmation for destructive actions.
Meet target size: at least 24×24 CSS px (WCAG 2.5.8) and aim for 44–48 px for primary controls.

AVOID.text: Do not use generic “OK”/“Submit” when the outcome can be named; never leave icon-only controls unnamed.
Do not use buttons for navigation or links for actions.

DECIDE.decision: Explicit verb plus confirmation or undo

EXAMPLE.good: “[Cancel] [Save changes]” with Save as the single primary action
EXAMPLE.bad: “[OK] [Submit]” or an icon-only trash button with no accessible name

FAILURE_MODES: Generic labels hide the consequence until after activation.
Icon-only controls are unnamed for screen-reader users.
Undersized or clustered targets cause misactivation on touch.
